https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/08/open.text: North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported on Tuesday, as Pyongyang gains advantages from its powerful neighbours Moscow and Beijing.The bridge over the Tumen river into Russia and an under-construction span to China are part of a shift that offers Western-sanctioned Pyongyang economic and strategic options it has long sought, experts said.North Korea "will simultaneously secure two major overland routes linking it with Russia and China, allowing it to encourage competition between the two countries and maximise its gains," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University.He noted the bridges also "can be a message to the United States that North Korea has no reason to beg Washington for sanctions relief or make concessions on denuclearisation in order to negotiate," Lim added.Russia noted the bridge is designed to accommodate expanded growth in freight with the capacity for up to 300 vehicles daily, which adds to the rail and air links already between the neighbours.Ukrainian rights group Truth Hounds, however, previously warned that the new bridge could become "a direct artery for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, with Russian technology and resources flowing in the opposite direction."The ceremony on Monday marking the new bridge's opening came as Russia and North Korea have heavily boosted military and economic ties since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.North Korea dispatched thousands of troops to Russia in 2024 to help ward off a Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region, while Kyiv has accused Moscow of using North Korean missiles in its regular barrages.South Korea's central bank estimated in July that North Korea's economy grew more than 3% for a third straight year in 2025, citing it's expansion of economic cooperation with Russia as a "major drive."The bank's official said North Korea's gross national income also "received a boost from a sharp rise in foreign currency earnings" linked to the deployment of its troops to Russia.Beijing-Moscow-Pyongyang bloc"The completion of the bridge is a significant event adding a new dynamic movement to the overall bilateral cooperation," North Korean official Pak Thae-song said in comments carried by the official KCNA news agency.North Korea and China are already connected by the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which is regularly used by passenger trains, but its capacity is limited.After a long halt, the bridge partly reopened and restored daily passenger train services with China earlier this year, but has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.North Korea has long kept tight control over foreign visitors and effectively sealed its borders at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic six years ago.The New Yalu River Bridge, intended as an alternative and eventual replacement of the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, is expected by experts to be completed this year.The completion of the bridge "sends a political and geopolitical message demonstrating the formation of a "North Korea-China-Russia continental triangular bloc," said Lim.

https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/.text: Front Page Taiwan News Business Editorial & Opinion Sports World News Features Bilingual Pages Search Search All Front Page Taiwan News Business Editorial & Opinion Sports World News Features Bilingual Pages GO Home Taiwan News Taiwan developing multilayered defense MULTIPLE FACTORS: Personnel, training, system integration and the ability to sustain combat readiness are essential to effective combat capabilities, the vice president said By Jake Chung / Staff writer, with CNA Add TT as Preferred Source Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim (蕭美琴) yesterday said Taiwan is working to bolster its defenses against rapidly evolving threats by developing multilayered air defenses, integrating emerging technologies and building a fully non-red drone supply chain. Taiwan has learned from the Russian invasion of Ukraine about the need for multilayered defenses and a rapid technology feedback loop to make cost-effective adjustments as threats and tactics evolve, she said at the Taipei Security Dialogue. The Middle East conflict has highlighted the importance of cost-effective air defense systems and counter-drone capabilities, she added. Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim speaks at the Taipei Security Dialogue yesterday. Photo: Tien Yu-hua, Taipei Times Artificial intelligence (AI) applications in intelligence analysis, target selection, interception and logistics warrant further study, she said. These lessons point to the need for the T-Dome project, which aims to link the detection and interception capabilities of a multilayered air defense network, Hsiao said. Its effectiveness would depend on integrating high-end and low-cost sensors and interceptors, AI-assisted rapid decisionmaking, trained operators and the ability to continue operating after severe damage, she added. Weapons delivery is only one step toward developing effective combat capabilities, Hsiao said, adding that personnel, training, system integration and the ability to sustain combat readiness are all essential. Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Taiwan Strait show that interference with maritime activity have economic effects far beyond coastal areas, making maritime domain awareness an increasingly important area of international cooperation, she said. Sharing intelligence with partners and using open-source intelligence tools, commercial satellite imagery, ship tracking data and other public information can improve situational awareness, identify threat patterns and document coercive activities, she said. The National Security Council and Ocean Affairs Council are working with international partners to identify ways to counter maritime coercion, Hsiao said, citing undersea cables — which carry communications supporting financial transactions, business operations and public services — as an example of infrastructure requiring protection. Taiwan’s strengths in semiconductors, information and communications technology, and precision manufacturing should be more closely linked to national defense, allowing military operators, researchers and companies to work together, Hsiao said. The government has submitted a special budget proposal for drone procurement, with coastal surveillance and reconnaissance drones, coastal attack drones and uncrewed attack boats to be domestically manufactured, she said. Drone production and procurement must use fully non-red supply chains, she added. Separately, Chiayi County Commissioner Weng Chang-liang (翁章梁), and representatives from Taiwan’s drone industry and research sectors visited Poland on Monday and signed a memorandum of understanding with the Pomerania Development Agency. Taiwan-Poland drone industry ties have deepened over the past few years, and Chiayi hopes to expand cooperation and enter new markets, Weng said. Chiayi began developing its drone industry in 2020 and is building a supply chain, from research and testing to manufacturing, he said. The agency said companies from both sides discussed drone manufacturing, systems integration, AI, uncrewed vehicles, defense technology and supply chains, seeking complementary capabilities and future business and technical cooperation. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmge.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, The busy training base is located behind fences on remote land in Alberta By Jack Burgess Published 18 October 2026, 18:48 BST Updated 21 minutes ago A huge fire swept through a Canadian military base on Saturday, killing at least four people and seriously injuring dozens more. Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as one of the worst peace time tragedies on Canadian soil in the history of the military. Here is what we know about the deadly incident so far. How did the fire start? Few details about what triggered the deadly fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which broke out at around 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT), have been confirmed by authorities so far. Local media reported it may have been started when a gas main was struck during a live firing exercise taking place on the grounds. Carney said a "violent, fast-moving fire swept through the base" without confirming what started it. Follow the latest updates The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had "spread rapidly due to high winds". The prime minister said military and civilian fire crews "fought this fire throughout the night in some of the worst conditions imaginable, risking their lives to protect their fellow Canadians". The Canadian defence ministry has said the cause remains under investigation, and "at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity". It has not been confirmed if those injured were on the base's sprawling ranges where exercises are carried out, or whether the fire spread to living quarters. Figure caption, Carney: 'Canada must now serve' service members killed in fire How many people have been killed? Four service members are confirmed to have died, Carney said on Sunday. He also said "dozens" had been "seriously wounded", without providing further information on their conditions. Prior to Carney addressing the nation, Canadian media reported the death toll as seven citing unnamed military sources. The prime minister did not indicate whether or not the government expects the death toll to rise. The names of those who lost their lives have not been identified but their families have been informed. On Saturday evening, Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton declared a code orange - a disaster response protocol for a high-casualty incident. It was stood down on Sunday afternoon. Alberta's health service said the emergency response lasted for 10 hours, and involved 22 ambulances and eight aircraft. Ongoing care for the injured is expected to be "intensive", a statement continued. A stream of ambulances were seen arriving at the hospital and one doctor told Canadian public broadcaster CBC that the facility had been "completely overwhelmed" by the number of patients. Where is the base? Canadian Forces Base Wainwright is located in a rural area of the western province of Alberta - around 120 miles (193km) from Edmonton and 180 miles (290km) from Calgary, the province's two largest cities. It is one of Canadian Army's busiest military training bases and its airfield is also used by the Royal Canadian Air Force. It population fluctuates but more than 1,000 people can be based there at any given time.
